arguments.independent_derivation:
I use LSV arXiv:math/0406217v2 Sections 2–4, not its later global Ramanujan claims. Set q=11 and d=3, E=F_(11^3), phi(a)=a^11, k=F_11(y), F=F_11((y)), O=F_11[[y]], R=F_11[y,1/y,1/(1+y)], R_T=F_11[y,1/(1+y)]. The cyclic k-algebra with z a=phi(a)z and z^3=1+y has dimension 9 over its center. Proposition 3.1, notably splitting at the y-adic place, embeds A(R) into M_3(F), with A(R_T) in M_3(O). Conjugation on the basis zeta_i z^j has scalar kernel; after quotienting scalars it is faithful (Section 3). This is an established substantial building theorem and algebra input, not independently reconstructed building theory.
LSV Section 2 defines the building using homothety classes of full lattices. Neighbors are intermediate lattices yL<L'<L and links are the flag complexes of the proper nonzero subspaces of F_11^3. Proposition 4.3 gives the q-index neighbors by b_u=u(1-z^-1)u^-1. Corollary 4.6 gives every q^2-index neighbor by b_u b_v. Thus all undirected neighbors, of BOTH types, are covered. Proposition 4.8 proves simple transitivity of Gamma. Definition 4.7 places Gamma inside GL_9(R_0), R_0=F_11[1/y], by the conjugation representation. Equation (9) has entries affine linear in t=1/y. Here A(R_0) is explicitly NOT defined, because R_0 does not contain R_T; the paper correctly reduces the matrix representation only. Membership in GL_9(R_0), and not merely matrices over R_0 invertible over its fraction field, ensures polynomial inverses. No incompatible irreducibility, reduced quotient, color-preserving subgroup, or global arithmetic spectral hypothesis is being silently imported.

For a path o=x_0,...,x_r=gamma o with r<=4, simple transitivity gives x_i=g_i o. Then g_(i-1)^-1 g_i takes o to an undirected neighbor and so is a positive product of at most two b_u. The word for gamma therefore has <=8 factors. Degree(rho(gamma))<=8. If gamma reduces to identity modulo t^9, each entry of rho(gamma)-I has degree <=8 and is divisible by t^9, hence is zero. Faithfulness implies gamma=1. Normality of the kernel lets this basepoint conclusion conjugate to every vertex. The finite target ring gives finite index. Since Gamma is vertex-regular, the orbit set is finite.
Defining the faces as the vertex-orbit images of actual faces gives an abstract downward-closed simplicial complex. Displacement>4 forbids an identification inside an edge/triangle and forbids two neighbors of x from sharing an orbit (distance at most 2). A quotient triangle containing [x] has an actual triangular lift with a vertex in [x]; translate the lift to x. Its remaining vertices are uniquely determined neighbors of x. Thus the graph on link vertices has exactly the lifted link edges, with no parallel triangles collapsed or new link edges added. The link is literally G, not only a quotient or a covering of G. Connectedness and purity descend. The stronger bound>4 is ample even though the immediate link injection needs only>2. No clique completion is used.

arguments.topic: Exact spectral estimate and deleted link
arguments.independent_derivation:
G has 133 points, 133 lines, degree 12; M M^T=11I+J. Since J has eigenvalues 133,0, the adjacency spectrum is +/-12 (simple) and +/-sqrt(11). The simple top eigenvalue, or elementary projective incidence, implies connectivity. Its ordinary Laplacian gap is 12-sqrt(11). No triangles occur because it is bipartite, and no 4-cycle occurs because distinct points determine a unique line; hence girth>=6.
For H=G-w and an unweighted-zero-mean vector x, append 0 at w. Its mean on G is still zero. E_G(x)=E_H(x)+sum_(u~w)x_u^2 <= E_H(x)+||x||^2, so E_H(x)>=(11-sqrt(11))||x||^2. In particular a disconnected H would admit a nonzero zero-mean componentwise-constant vector and violate this inequality, proving connectivity. For any f, subtract its UNWEIGHTED mean to get x, preserving E_H. The degree-weighted minimum variance D(f)=min_c sum d_H(u)(f_u-c)^2 is <=sum d_H(u)x_u^2<=12||x||^2. Therefore E_H(f)/D(f)>=(11-sqrt(11))/12>7/12>1/2, using sqrt(11)<4. The inequality is in the correct direction: an upper bound on the denominator is what gives the lower bound on the ratio. No assumption that H is regular is made. G itself has normalized gap 1-sqrt(11)/12>1/2.

A finite pure 2-complex has m(e)>0 on every edge, giving a positive definite edge inner product. A cohomology class in Z^1/B^1 has an energy-minimizing representative a by orthogonal projection to B^1. Varying the representative by the vertex delta coboundary makes sum_(u)m(vu)a_vu=0 for each v; signs depend on the antisymmetric convention but the equation is zero. The local function f_v(u)=a_vu therefore has zero degree-weighted mean, since degree of u in lk(v) equals m(vu). The cocycle equation on v,u,w gives f_v(u)-f_v(w)=-a_uw. Summing the link energies counts every edge uw once for each incident triangle, giving exactly E(a). Summing the corresponding local weighted squared norms counts every oriented incidence vu, giving exactly 2E(a). A common minimum lambda>1/2 among finitely many link gaps gives E(a)>=2lambda E(a), hence E(a)=0 and H^1=0. This is not an invocation of property (T) alone. The strict inequality matters: at equality a nonzero class is possible (the triangulated torus control will be checked in Phase 3).

arguments.topic: Every deletion and every Reisner case
arguments.independent_derivation:
Each edge lies in 12 triangles, since its endpoint is a link vertex of degree 12. Deleting z removes at most one of those triangles, since the complex is abstract; every surviving edge remains in at least 11 triangles. Every surviving vertex originally has 266 distinct neighbors and loses at most one, so it has a surviving edge and then a surviving triangle. Hence K-z is nonempty, pure and of dimension 2. A path that uses z can be replaced through the connected link G of z, and those link edges survive; this proves connectivity of K-z. For any v!=z, its new link is exactly G if vz was absent and G-w if present. The cocycle result gives H^1=0 in K and K-z. Over R, finite-dimensional cochain/chain duality gives H_1=0; integer matrix ranks are unchanged over Q, R, or any characteristic-zero field, giving the same conclusion there.
At the empty face the nonempty connected complex has Htilde_-1=Htilde_0=0 and H_1=0; these are all below dimension 2. At a vertex, its nonempty connected graph link has Htilde_-1=Htilde_0=0 below dimension 1. At an edge, its nonempty 0-dimensional link has Htilde_-1=0. A triangle has link {empty}, dimension -1, with no below-top obligation. Dimensions of all deletions agree with K. Thus all 2-CM conditions over characteristic zero, not merely global H_1 vanishing, have been verified.

Let S be a 2-dimensional k-homology sphere subcomplex, with the local convention stated explicitly in Swartz Section 4 and consistent with Nevo. At an edge e, lk_S(e) is a finite 0-complex with Htilde_0 dimension 1, so it has exactly two vertices; each edge lies in two triangles. For v in S, lk_S(v) is connected by its reduced H_0, and each of its vertices has degree 2 by the edge condition. It is therefore a simple cycle. As a subgraph of G the cycle has length>=6. Hence 2f_1=sum_v deg_S(v)>=6f_0 and 3f_2=2f_1, giving chi(S)=f_0-f_1/3<=0. Global k-sphere homology instead gives chi=2 by the Euler–Poincare identity over any field. No orientability or surface-classification argument, inducedness, subdivision or positive-characteristic 2-CM claim is required.
A global homology S^2 complex without local sphere links need not satisfy this degree-two argument. The paper expressly disclaims that weaker use of the term. The original Theorem 7/3.4 asks for subcomplex pieces in K of the original dimension; absence of even one permitted sphere precludes a cover and all overlap/reordering conditions. The characteristic-zero example, in particular Q, negates the universal field-parametrized question.

I attempted to falsify polynomial reduction by using the wrong algebra base, noninvertible polynomial matrices, an uncovered reverse neighbor, characteristic restrictions, or the nonreduced t^9 target; all are resolved by the exact LSV scope above. I attempted quotient foldings/spurious triangles, low-dimensional deletion maximal faces, disconnected deletions/links, a reversed weighted denominator estimate, an erroneous energy factor, the strict-boundary equality, and all-field sphere-orientability exceptions. None gives a counterexample to the argument as written. The mathematical claim is valid conditional on the cited established building/conjugation facts.
